name: Bristol
description: Bristol is a patience (solitaire) card game played with a single standard 52-card deck. It is a fan-type layout in the style of La Belle Lucie, with building regardless of suit on both the foundations and the tableau, and is considered relatively easy to win.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: United States
Time Period: Around 1950
Historical Development: Invented by the card game authors Morehead and Mott-Smith as a fan-type patience closely related to La Belle Lucie.
Cultural Significance: Known as an easy-to-win solitaire, included in classic card game collections.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

rules.objective: Be the first player to achieve the winning condition through strategic play of cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. Setup: prepare players, deck or tiles, and opening layout according to the variant. 2. Turn loop: each player performs one legal action (play, capture, build, bet, or pass/draw as applicable). 3. Resolution: each action updates control of tricks/cards/pot/layout. 4. End condition: when hand-ending criteria are met, scoring is computed and match state advances.
keyRules: Play proceeds in turn order with only legal actions allowed.
Round resolution follows the variant's scoring and bonus conditions.
Match winner is determined by agreed target score or elimination condition.

strategy.basic: Bristol: follow rules; strategy depends on variant.
strategy.intermediate: Track revealed information (cards, tiles, tricks, or betting patterns) and adjust plan as opponent ranges narrow.
strategy.advanced: Use tempo and denial lines to convert small positional edges into scoring swings in late hand phases.
tips: Fix the exact local variant before play so edge cases are predictable.
Plan two turns ahead: most mistakes come from giving opponents forced value.
Recalculate risk near end-of-hand scoring thresholds.

variations.name: Belvedere
variations.description: Belvedere is a closely related patience in which an ace is removed from the deck before the deal and immediately set up as a foundation, but play otherwise follows the normal rules of Bristol.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine-level overrides are not modeled yet; Belvedere shares Bristol's structure with only the starting foundation rule changed.

variations.name: House rules and table variants
variations.description: Players sometimes adjust small details such as redeal limits or whether gaps in the tableau may be filled, but core Bristol structure and building rules stay the same.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Specific engine overrides for informal house rules are not standardized or encoded; they are described textually only.

synthesis.shortDescription: Bristol is a patience card game that involves tableau, foundations, stock. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.
